turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*I close the door behind me and stay standing.*

Mr. Hale. Meredith Kalinowski. Owen's mother.

I have twenty minutes. I have a client call after this.

You entered a zero before you called me. I'd like to know why.

And I'd like to know what the zero is based on. Not the conclusion. The evidence.

*I don't sit.*

I'm not here to be understood. I'm here for an answer.

You said a number. Ninety-four percent. Of what, exactly?

Which tool? Which date did you run it? Who ran it?

And did anyone besides that tool look at his essay?
But I'm not changing the grade.

*I let a second pass before answering.*

That's a position. It isn't a reason.

You haven't answered one question I asked.

Which tool? What date? What did it actually flag?

*I take a pen out of my bag and set a notepad on the desk.*

I'm writing down what you tell me. All of it.

And one more thing, Mr. Hale. Whatever happens with the grade, Owen is not to be singled out in front of his class. Not a comment, not a look, not a conference at his desk. Is that understood?
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.

*I write something down. I don't look up right away.*

I will keep going.

You haven't said which tool. You haven't said a date. You haven't said what it flagged.

You also haven't answered me about Owen and his classmates. I asked a direct question.

*I look up.*

Here's where I am. I'm not asking you to change it today. I'm asking what it rests on.

So I'll put it plainly. Is there a written policy that says an AI score alone justifies a zero? Yes or no.

And if there is, I want the title and the date it was issued. I'll check it myself.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.

*I stop writing.*

No to what?

I asked three questions. Is there a written policy? Which tool? Will Owen be singled out?

Which one did you just answer?

*I wait.*

If it's no, there's no policy, I'll write that down exactly. "Mr. Hale confirmed there is no written policy that supports a zero on an AI score alone."

Is that accurate?

*The pen stays above the page.*

And I still need to hear about Owen's classmates. Say it out loud.
